instructions: Heat the oven to 300°F with a rack in the lower third.
Meanwhile, toast the 1/4 cup pine nuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until they're golden and smell nutty. Transfer them into a mixing bowl.
Mince 2 of the garlic cloves and thinly slice the other 2, keeping them in separate piles. Chop 1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp of the parsley. Finely grate the Parmesan and finely chop the onion.

Add the minced garlic, 1/4 cup of the chopped parsley, the Parmesan, the 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, the 1/4 cup raisins and 2 tbsp of the olive oil to the pine nuts. Mix until it's evenly damp, like wet sand.

Lay the steak flat on a board. If it's thicker than 1/2 inch, slice it through the middle sideways, stopping short of the far edge, and open it out like a book. Cover it with plastic wrap and pound it with a meat mallet or a rolling pin to an even 1/4 inch.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper over both sides. Spread the filling over the top, leaving a 1/2 inch border, and press it down with your palm.
Starting from a short end, roll the steak up tightly, tucking in any filling that falls out. Tie it with kitchen twine every 1 1/2 inches.

Pat the outside dry with paper towels. Heat the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium high until it shimmers. Add the roll and brown it for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, turning it with tongs, until it's deep brown all over. Transfer it onto a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the onion. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft. Add the sliced garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the 1/2 cup wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Let it bubble for about 2 minutes, until it has cooked down by half.

Add the 2 cans of tomatoes with their juice and crush them against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon. Add the bay leaf and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper and bring it to a simmer. Put the roll back in with any juices from the plate and spoon some sauce over it.
Put the lid on and move the pot to the oven. Cook for 1 hour.
Turn the roll over and cook it uncovered for 1 hour, until a fork slides into the meat easily and the sauce has thickened. If it still feels firm, give it another 30 minutes.
About 20 minutes before the braciole is done, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the 1 lb rigatoni until it's tender with a little bite, following the package time, then drain it.
Lift the roll onto a board and let it rest for 10 minutes. Fish the bay leaf out of the sauce.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Toss the rigatoni with about half the sauce.
Snip off the twine and cut the roll into 1 inch slices. Spoon the rest of the sauce over the slices and scatter the 2 tbsp parsley on top. Serve with the rigatoni.
method_notes: Both pound a flank steak thin, spread it with a breadcrumb, garlic, Parmesan and olive oil filling, roll and tie it, brown it in a Dutch oven and braise it in tomato sauce until it's fork tender. Scarlati Family Kitchen keeps the filling plain with Italian seasoning, uses 4 cups of ready Sunday gravy and braises at 300°F in the oven for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, half covered and half uncovered. ColeyCooks adds toasted pine nuts, golden raisins and parsley to the filling, builds the sauce in the same pot from onion, garlic, red wine and crushed whole tomatoes with a bay leaf, and simmers it on the stove for about 3 hours. Neither had 20 ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no braciole, so this follows Scarlati's oven braise with ColeyCooks' filling and sauce, doubled to 2 cans so there's enough to dress a pound of rigatoni.
